## Today

1. From one predictor to many
2. Judging the fit

## [Section 1]{.section-kicker} From one predictor to many {.section-slide background-color="#002f57"}

## The model

::: {.subtitle-frame}
One line, then a semester of consequences
:::

$$
y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{i1} + \dots + \beta_p x_{ip} + \varepsilon_i,
\qquad \varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)
$$

- Each $\beta_j$ is the effect of $x_j$ *holding the others fixed*
- [That clause]{.gold} is the whole difference from simple regression
- Estimated by least squares, exactly as before: $\hat\beta = (X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top y$

## In R

```{.r code-line-numbers="1|2|3"}
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp + qsec, data = mtcars)
summary(fit)          # coefficients, standard errors, R^2
confint(fit)          # 95% intervals for each beta
```

::: {.callout-note}
`summary()` tests each coefficient against zero *given the others*. A variable that is significant alone can vanish once its correlates enter.
:::

## Adding a predictor never lowers $R^2$. {.statement}

[That is why $R^2$ cannot choose a model.]{.muted}

## [Section 2]{.section-kicker} Judging the fit {.section-slide background-color="#002f57"}

## Adjusted $R^2$ and beyond

::: {.callout-tip title="Adjusted R²"}
$\bar R^2 = 1 - (1 - R^2)\,\dfrac{n-1}{n-p-1}$ — penalises $p$ so that an irrelevant predictor lowers it.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Before the lab"}
Fit `mpg ~ .` on `mtcars`, then drop predictors one at a time. Watch $R^2$ and $\bar R^2$ move in different directions.
:::
